citation.title: Deep learning-aided topology design of metasurfaces for Rayleigh waves
citation.authors: Cheng Zhao; Chen-Xu Liu; Gui-Lan Yu
citation.venue: Journal of Computational Design and Engineering, vol. 11, issue 3, pp. 56-71 (Oxford University Press; open access, CC BY-NC 4.0)
citation.version_coded: Version of record (open access), full text read from https://academic.oup.com/jcde/article/11/3/56/7649376. The adjudicator re-read it on 2026-09-24 as the publisher PDF (16 pp.): the open-access article page was served to WebFetch without a challenge, and its PDF link (academic.oup.com/jcde/article-pdf/11/3/56/57387741/qwae037.pdf) redirected to the publisher's own PDF server (watermark02.silverchair.com); the PDF was read in full as text, including the Appendix

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (excluded). Headline: a VAE compresses discrete metasurface topologies into a continuous latent space, and a conditional tandem neural network designs latent vectors to hit target Rayleigh-wave bandgaps under varying soil conditions, validated on 100 test cases (R2 > 0.99, mean relative error 1.5%, about 5.4 s per design); no classical (gradient-based or evolutionary) optimizer is run, timed, or cited with a specific cost for this problem.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (excluded at full text). No classical-method run time is stated or cited anywhere in the article. The only timing contrast (Sec. 5.1, p. 63) sets the full VAE+cTNN pipeline (about 5.4 s per design) against the same design model without the VAE, which the authors say fails to reach a required topology within several hours: an internal ablation, not a classical, non-learned comparator.

notes: Excluded under PROTOCOL §4 and the 2026-09-24 FT-NOBASELINE clarification: the article never runs, times, or cites a specific cost or result of a classical (non-learned) optimization method on this design problem. Codes checked in closed-list order: FT-DUPLICATE does not apply (pool.csv holds one record for this title and DOI). FT-SCOPE does not apply: inverse topology design of a metamaterial unit cell (metasurface), which the authors call a DL-based topology optimization method. FT-TYPE does not apply (research article). FT-DOMAIN does not apply: Rayleigh (elastic surface) waves in soil are elastodynamics in solids, in scope per the §11 physics-scope clarification ('acoustic' means sound in fluids). FT-NOML does not apply (VAE and cTNN). FT-FORWARD does not apply: the cTNN's inverse network is updated by gradient descent to design latent vectors and periodic constants (Sec. 4.2, 4.4), so the ML does inverse design, not only forward prediction. FT-MLONLY does not apply: no other ML method is run or benchmarked; the with/without-VAE contrast of Sec. 5.1 is an internal ablation (as in P00335), and the MLP-plus-GA and conditional-GAN approaches appear only as qualitative literature (Introduction, para. 3). FT-NOBASELINE applies: Introduction para. 2 (p. 56) names level-set and genetic-algorithm design of metasurfaces and says only, citing generic references (Nesterov & Spokoiny 2017; Nguyen et al. 2022), that each design needs much computation and time, the qualitative 'TO is slow' motivation the clarification excludes. The Fig. 3 check against Z. Liu et al. (2021) validates the forward dispersion computation, not an optimization result, and the 85% acceleration reduction of Sec. 5.3 compares the designed metasurfaces with no metasurface. Datasets: 300,000 rule-generated topologies (Dataset A, no FE required) and 80,000 samples with bandgaps computed by FE simulation in COMSOL Multiphysics 5.4 (Dataset B); no generation time or cost, training time, or hardware (CPU/GPU) is stated anywhere for either dataset or for network training. Design outputs are checked against target bandgaps and validated on 100 held-out cases (R2 0.996 and 0.998 for the lower and upper edges, mean relative error 1.5%, Sec. 5.1), but no failure or infeasibility rate is reported. No code or data availability statement is given. No author named Jun Wang (authors: Cheng Zhao, Chen-Xu Liu, Gui-Lan Yu). Screening code was I-UNCLEAR. Adjudication (2026-09-24): the first coder met the Cloudflare check on academic.oup.com and kept the screening decision for lack of full text; the adjudicator reached the full text through the open-access article page and the publisher's PDF server, so the full-text exclusion of the second coding stands. The second coding's long verbatim quotations in the notes were replaced by paraphrases (PROTOCOL §7.4).

access.reason: The open-access article page (academic.oup.com/jcde/article/11/3/56/7649376, CC BY-NC) was served without a challenge, and its PDF link redirects to the publisher's own PDF server, which PROTOCOL §11 counts as accessible; the adjudicator read the 16-page PDF in full. The first coder's scripted requests met a Cloudflare check and correctly stopped.

decision.reason: With the full text readable, the no-full-text rule no longer holds the screening include. The article runs, times or cites no classical optimizer's cost or result: level-set and GA design appear only as qualitative motivation (Introduction para. 2, p. 56), and the only timing contrast is an internal with/without-VAE ablation (Sec. 5.1, p. 63).

ft_code.reason: Earlier codes fail: the problem is metamaterial inverse topology design in an elastic solid (in scope under the §11 elastic-wave clarification), the ML does inverse design (Sec. 4.2, 4.4), and no other ML method is benchmarked, since the no-VAE contrast (Sec. 5.1) is an internal ablation, as in P00335. The first applicable code in table order is FT-NOBASELINE.
